L3.1.quote: Indeed, if Liu always takes a longest remaining piece, then before his $k$-th turn at most $2k-2$ pieces have disappeared, so the piece he takes has length at least $x_{2k-1}$. Thus he secures at least $O$.
L3.1.note: Both greedy strategies written out; odd-sum game value and O=(1+Delta)/2 proved for all n.

L3.2.quote: With $s$ cuts available and at most $s+1$ columns of total height $T$, sweep a horizontal line down through them, recording successive vertical portions alternately in two rows (according as the number of columns met is odd or even). Set $d=T/(2^{s+1}-1)$.
L3.2.note: Lemma (i) states the right all-n statement, but the sweep proof leaves cut choice, cancellation, array bounds, and induction unjustified; sketch only.

L3.3.quote: At $j=s$, the second possibility requires at least $s+1$ cuts. With at most $s$ cuts, an odd strip therefore remains, and (5) gives $\Delta\ge d$. This proves (ii).
L3.3.note: Strip-sweep induction for Lemma (ii) is sketched for all n, but the invariant, 'identical copies' step, and cut-count claim are asserted, not proven.

parsed.notes: Reduction (L3.1) fully proved; closed form 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) correctly stated as the answer. Both bounds rest on the refinement lemma, whose parts are only sketched: cancellation, array totals, and induction transfer are asserted without proof, so neither bound is established.
